- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to counteract bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If model consistently forecasts below true price with no sentiment signal, assume mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next period.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend (not 30-day).  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 5 days, model often underreacts; forecast should rise 1–2% faster than sentiment suggests.
